pattern-selector.why: the forces were: a new end-of-task precondition, one owner of 'covered' already exists (esk-genesis --check), and false blocks must be impossible; the fit is to add one more precondition that DELEGATES the verdict, deliberately no new subsystem or second owner.
pattern-selector.what: added coverageProblems() as orchestration that delegates the covered/drift verdict to esk-genesis --check and joins the existing missing[] path; recorded the rejected options (separate hook, nudge-only, bot-only) in ADR-0116.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: making coverage a finish-check precondition is a decision a maintainer will question (why in finish-check, why delegate, why a TTL waiver, why skip the upstream).
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0116 (the structural/judgment split, the adoption gate, delegation to esk-genesis --check, the TTL waiver, the honest limits), referencing ADR-0115/0110.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the coverage behaviour across audiences (agent, operator, subagent) and non-happy paths (ungated, drift, fail-closed, lapsed waiver, self-waive, read-only, upstream) is enumerated as Gherkin and logged, then executed in CI.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added features/always-on/coverage-precondition.feature (11 scenarios) + steps driving the real finish-check against fixtures, and a bdd-coverage-log entry; runs under npm run test:bdd.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the defect class is the Stop-hook decision, so the test drives the real finish-check end to end against fixture repos in each coverage state, not a unit of the predicate.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added test/finish-check-coverage.test.mjs (11 cases: non-adopted/covered/ungated/workflow/drift/fail-closed/waiver/lapse/never-expire/self-waive/upstream), driving the real hook.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: a coverage check that went blind would ship green, so its tests must fail when the check is neutralized.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: mutation pass: forced coverageProblems() to return [] and confirmed the 6 blocked cases red while the 4 pass-cases stay green; reverted; recorded in the review entry and the test header.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the claim 'structurally impossible to end without authorization' was disconfirmed by the block-cap escalation (after N blocks the turn ends), so the honest guarantee is 'impossible to end SILENTLY; escalates as a recorded decision'; the drift verdict's topology-dependence was also named.
skeptical-audit.what: recorded the corrected guarantee and the named limits (binds Claude-driven work only; escalation ceiling; version-skew topology; forged-waiver visibility) in ADR-0116's 'what this does not fix'.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: the change edits the enforcement engine, so it got a fresh-context four-question review over every changed file before done.
judge-arch.what: dispatched a fresh-context subagent that returned the full matrix + grep battery; verdict PASS with 4 low findings (2 fixed, 2 waived with reasons); review recorded.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the simplest thing that meets the requirement is one delegated precondition reusing esk-genesis --check and the existing waiver/escalation machinery, not a second gate that re-derives coverage.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: kept coverage to one orchestration function with one owner of 'covered'; reused the operator-waiver file and the block-cap escalation; documented the group in finish-check-records.md.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the change parses an operator-writable waiver file and spawns a child process, so it was threat-modeled from the attacker's view: self-waive forgery, spawn injection, and untrusted date/reason content.
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: enforced agent-cannot-self-waive (only by:'operator' entries with a reason count), an injection-safe spawn (argument array, no shell, no string built from file content), and fail-closed waiver parsing (Date.parse only; missing/future/unparseable date does not count); shipped the @security scenario coverage-agent-cannot-self-waive.
quotes: so you defend against what attackers actually do, not an abstract risk

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, or production rollout; a session-time Stop-hook precondition over local files.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, retention, or migration; it reads marker/manifest existence and an operator waiver file locally.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, endpoint, SLO, or alert; a build/session-time hook.

arch-encode.why: the caught mistake (the upstream repo self-blocking, and the single-file upstream heuristic) is locked by committed discriminating tests (coverage-upstream-exempt + the tightened two-file signal), not a source-pattern grep rule for the arch-gate.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; a Node hook.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user UI; the block message names the gap and the fix (run esk-genesis --yes, or record an operator coverage waiver) in plain words.
